idiom_name: thin view/main + plain function or service object (pytest, unittest.mock)
implementation_notes: Python's plain-function style replaces the humble class: the Django view or command-line main reads the request or arguments, calls a module-level function or small service object with plain data, and renders or reports the result, so pytest drives the logic without a web server. unittest.mock's patch installs doubles in the namespace where the name is looked up, which keeps the shell's delegation testable without a container, while the Django test client and RequestFactory cover the thin view when it needs checking. Keep the framework class where it genuinely carries framework behaviour (forms, permissions), but move the decisions out of it.
pitfalls: Patching the wrong namespace: patch replaces the name where it is looked up, so patching the defining module leaves the view calling the real dependency (the documented where-to-patch rule).
Passing the request or other framework globals into the logic re-imports the environment; pass plain data so tests need no request object.
Import-time side effects (settings access, app registry) make a module untestable even when the function is pure; keep framework imports at the shell.
